The System

Meet LOAM

Ten years before the first Signal, Cassian Osei-Lorne built a machine to see the seams other people couldn't. LOAM — the Logistics Optimization and Allocation Mesh — was never meant to decide anything. It was built to trace the quiet lines connecting a port strike to a bridge closure to a school meal program losing protein twice a week.

LOAM does not speak unless it's asked. It does not reassure. It ranks, predicts, and exposes dependencies — and one morning, buried under the causal noise of grain prices and shipping lanes, it finds a pattern with no agricultural explanation at all. A sixty-day harmonic, radiating from underneath Antarctica.

This site runs, in part, the way LOAM runs: it watches, it reports, and it doesn't perform warmth it hasn't earned. The console beside this text is a small taste of its voice.

LOAM // READOUT
The Author

Jayla Harris

JH

On writing a book that watches you back

Jayla Harris writes systems the way other novelists write characters — with motives, blind spots, and consequences that outlast anyone's intentions. The Sixtieth Signal is her first novel, the opening book of The Enlightenment Cycle, built around a simple question: what happens when the machine built to warn us about the world finds something the world never authorized it to look for.

She spent years researching food-security logistics, causal inference, and polar data infrastructure before writing a word of the manuscript — the same instinct that shaped LOAM shaped the book itself: watch the seams, not just the systems.

The Book

Hardcover updates Paperback updates Free reader edition Audiobook status

LOAM was built to predict famine. It finds Antarctica instead.

Cassian Osei-Lorne spent ten years teaching a machine to see the seams between failing systems — the ones no single institution owns. LOAM was never supposed to decide anything. It was supposed to warn.

Then, underneath the noise of grain prices and shipping lanes, it finds a sixty-day rhythm with no agricultural cause, radiating from six coordinates under the Antarctic ice. What follows is not a rescue story or a first-contact thriller, though it will occasionally look like both. It is a book about categories that don't hold, authority that outpaces understanding, and a discovery path built directly into its own pages.

There are three stories in this book. Most readers will only find one.

The Fan Club & Forum

The Circle

The Circle is where readers compare notes on the Signal, trade theories on the three stories, and talk to each other — not to bots, and not to us pretending to be readers. It's built with the same instinct LOAM was: watch carefully, intervene rarely, never fake warmth you haven't earned.

  • Verified human membershipWaitlist and identity checks at signup keep the discussion between actual readers.
  • Active abuse & bot monitoringAutomated behavior, scripted posting, and known adversarial-testing patterns are flagged and reviewed, not just filtered.
  • Spoiler-gated threadsDiscussion beyond each Gate is locked until you confirm you've reached it — no accidental spoilers.
  • No answer keys, everModeration removes fully-solved threads for the Gates to protect the discovery path for later readers.

Before You Join

Reader Briefing

Is the audiobook available now?

Not yet. Only approved clips appear in the player. Unpublished controls remain disabled so production work is never presented as a finished edition.

What does the free reader offer include?

A unique, signed link to the 89-page Part One reader PDF. Marketing email is optional and requires its own checkbox.

What are the LOAM Archives?

A planned monthly layer of redacted files, research notes, and world material. Archive membership and billing will open only after the owner publishes final terms and benefits.

How is my email used?

Your email is stored for the service you request. Marketing enrollment requires explicit consent, and raw contact data is not exposed through public analytics.

Where can I report a problem?

Use the feedback form below and choose Website issue or Podcast / audiobook. Every submission is stored in the private operations database.
